svg.text: PART 8: CLOCK AND TANK SENSOR ON THE I2C BUS
Test setup for step 3. Only the laptop USB is needed: both parts run on 3.3 V from the Nucleo.
USB cable to the laptop (power and code)
pins in row a, columns 29 to 34,
in the tank lid, facing the food,
joined with 4 female to male wires
peel off the thin film on the sensor
I2C bus, bottom half: column 31 = SCL (white wires),
column 32 = SDA (blue wires). Every part plugs into these two.
Column map of the whole feeder:
3.3 V: Nucleo 3V3 to the bottom + rail; VCC, VIN
Tank sensor: 4 pins only, VIN GND SCL SDA
EEPROM 0x57 (on the clock board, not used)
Pull up resistors are on the modules: none added
Idle check: SDA and SCL both read 3.3 V
1. Wire everything with the USB unplugged.
2. Both parts on 3.3 V, never on 5 V.
3. The coin cell keeps the time without power.
4. At 3.3 V the clock board needs no change.
5. Tank sensor: nothing in front but the food.
6. Check every Nucleo pin label before plugging.
Kibbly hardware · circuit 8 of the circuits by part · wires I1 to I15 in hardware/04_wiring_list.md section 9, rails R2 and R3 in section 4B
